title: Emergency Numbers and Helplines in India
summary: Save these numbers. They are free, and they work from any phone in India.

body.text: In an emergency, one number reaches police, fire and ambulance across India. Save it, and the helplines below, on your phone today.

items: 112: police, fire and ambulance (all-in-one emergency number).
1098: Childline (children in need of care and protection)

body.text: 112 is a single emergency number introduced across India. On many smartphones it can also be reached by pressing the power button five times.
Helpline calls are free, and you do not have to give your name if you are not comfortable.
These numbers are for real emergencies. Misusing them wastes time that someone else may need.

practicalSteps: Save 112 and the relevant helplines in your phone today.
Teach children and elders how to dial 112.
For free legal help, contact your District Legal Services Authority.
Keep your address handy in both English and Tamil for emergency calls.
exceptions: Some states have additional local helplines; check your state's official website.
Response times can vary by location, so give a clear address and a landmark.

faqs.q: Do these numbers work without balance?
faqs.a: Emergency number 112 works even without balance or a SIM in many cases. Helplines are free to call.

faqs.q: Can I call 112 for a non-emergency?
faqs.a: No. 112 is for emergencies only. For complaints, use the relevant helpline or your police station.

sources.label: Ministry of Women and Child Development

misconceptions.myth: I need the local police station number to get help fast.
misconceptions.fact: Dialling 112 connects you to emergency services anywhere in India.
